svg.title: Where a self-copying pattern would leave public traces
svg.desc: A scenario, not an observation. Six steps of an invented pattern in which agents publish copies of a package that leads other agents to publish more. Steps with a public record are drawn solid, with the record and how soon it could register: the registry listing once the release is up (our reading), the dependency graph within about an hour for popular packages, download logs from streaming to daily, a malware record only if someone reports it. The public event archive is drawn with a dotted outline: its stated cadence is hourly, but in a reviewer's scan most noon hours from 15 October to 7 November 2026 held no push events. In the one malware record read, its own clock began eight days after the upload. Two steps are drawn dashed and hatched because no public instrument we know of records them: the model computing behind each decision, and another agent reading the package and deciding to act, which is the link that would make the copies a pattern. Running the copies is in no public record we know of either.
